adhd/neurodivergent.title: Feels More Focused on Revenue Than User Experience
adhd/neurodivergent.content:
This was recommended by a ADHD youtuber, so I tried the Endel app after his recommendation. Unfortunately, my experience was the opposite of what I expected.
The subscription model was the first red flag. Even though I downloaded it through the App Store, I had to enter my credit card directly instead of subscribing through Apple. If someone forgets to cancel the 7-day trial, they’re charged $119 for a year. I only used the app for a few minutes before deciding it wasn’t for me and canceled right away, but the whole setup felt intentionally designed to make it easier for people to end up paying.

Before I even had a chance to understand what the app actually did, it was asking me to invite three friends. That immediately gave me the impression that getting new users is a higher priority than letting people experience the product first (which also hints that the developers are not very confident in the product itself, because if the product was great, people would recommend it to friends and family without prompting)

The app is also marketed for people with ADHD, but I found the interface overwhelming rather than helpful. There are lots of menus and options to click through without much guidance. I tapped “Anxiety Relief,” expecting some explanation or immediate experience, but it simply asked me to set a timer. Then I was looking at a black screen with a few dots and, at least in my case, no sound at all. I was left wondering whether I had missed something. Instead of feeling supported, I felt confused.

Overall, the app felt like a basic library of ambient sounds with very little explanation of what makes it worth $119 a year. The black screen with gray and white elements also felt claustrophobic to me rather than calming. I kept wondering what I was paying for that I couldn’t get elsewhere.

What I found most ironic is that this app was recommended in a video about doing less and avoiding unnecessary additions to your life. To me, this app is exactly that—another subscription, another account, another thing to manage, without offering enough value to justify it.

adhd/neurodivergent.title: Warning: $119.99 billing trap
adhd/neurodivergent.content:
I strongly recommend avoiding this app unless you are prepared to risk a $119.99 charge that may not appear under your normal Apple Subscriptions.

My issue is not just that the app is overpriced. The issue is the billing flow. I downloaded Endel believing I was starting a free trial. I did not knowingly agree to a paid annual subscription or knowingly authorize a $119.99 charge. After the charge appeared, I immediately checked my Apple Subscriptions to cancel or manage it, but there was no active or past Endel subscription listed there.

That matters. Most iPhone users reasonably assume that if they download an app from the App Store and authorize payment through an Apple-looking flow, the subscription will appear under Apple Subscriptions. In my case, it did not. That means I could not cancel, verify, or manage the charge through the standard Apple subscription process.

This is especially concerning because Endel markets itself toward people with ADHD and focus difficulties. A confusing trial/payment/cancellation flow is bad for any user, but it is especially harmful when the app is being advertised to people who may already struggle with memory, task-switching, and subscription management.

The ads I saw also emphasized special “8D” audio/music content. What I found in the app did not match what was advertised. Other reviews describe similar issues: people expected the advertised 8D tracks or trial experience and instead ended up confused, disappointed, or charged.

If you already got charged and cannot find Endel under Apple Subscriptions, this is the dispute language I recommend giving your bank or card issuer:

“I am disputing a $119.99 charge from Endel. I did not knowingly authorize a paid annual subscription and did not provide informed consent to be charged this amount. I initially downloaded the Endel app under what was presented as a free trial. After seeing the charge, I immediately attempted to locate and cancel any associated subscription. However, there is no active or past Endel subscription listed under my Apple Subscriptions. Because the subscription does not appear in Apple’s subscription management system, I was unable to cancel, verify, or manage it through the normal Apple subscription process. For these reasons, I believe this charge resulted from a deceptive or unclear billing flow, and I request a full refund.”

This app should not be allowed to advertise a simple free-trial experience while using a payment and cancellation structure that many users cannot reasonably understand or manage. Be extremely careful before entering any trial or payment flow.

Unfortunately, after subscribing, I found that there was only one 8D sound available. There really isn’t much variety to choose from, and I also feel like the Focus, Sleep, and Relaxation options all sound very similar.
What made the experience even more disappointing is that, despite purchasing a yearly subscription, every time I open the app I’m bombarded with promotions asking me to purchase a lifetime subscription. It’s frustrating to pay for a full year and still constantly feel like I’m being advertised to and pushed to spend more money.
Overall, the app just wasn’t what I expected based on the advertising. I was hoping for a much wider selection of immersive sounds and more variety between the different modes. For the price, I expected a lot more.

sleep.title: AirPlay now broken
sleep.content:
I am changing my review from one star to five stars. Endel ‘Sleep’ once again works flawlessly when streaming via AirPlay to my HomePod. Its abysmally fitful AirPlay performance of the past couple of months appears to have been definitively resolved by some software updates — iOS to 26.4, HomePod OS to 26.4, and Endel to 4.7.10. 
  For years, I had played Endel “Sleep” at night on a HomePod via AirPlay from my iPhone. This became no longer reliable. Playback of “Sleep” to the HomePod stopped within 5 minutes. It then might work in fits and starts a couple of times, then cut out completely. My hardware is solid, so this was due solely to Endel software changes. I suspect it is related to Endel periodically “refreshing” its audio session, and that a recent Endel update (or iOS/macOS update) made those refreshes more aggressive. AirPlay is intolerant of this, and just quits.

sleep.title: Ein wirklich gelungenes Programm
sleep.content:
Die App verbindet die physischen Daten des Nutzers (wenn eine Smartwatch benutzt wird) mit den kosmischen (zirkardianrhythmisch) - und zwar regionalspezifisch (Wetterapp und Standortdaten). Sie spielt Klänge über einen Synthesizer ab. Vier Klangprogramme bilden die eingespeisten Daten ab. Dabei gibt es vier frei wählbare Klangvarianten - je nachdem, was man erreichen will: Beruhigung (Rest) Konzentration (Fokus), Ab- oder Anspannung (Go to) und schließlich Schlaf (Sleep). Es gibt im Internet eine Variante mit Gesang. Die sollte in die App integriert werden. Interessant wäre sicher auch die Kopplung mit einem Emotions-/ Gehirnwellensensor (Stirnband). Drittens schlage ich vor, dass ein Expertenmodus eingebaut wird, der Nutzungsempfehlungen und Verhaltensempfehlungen sowie persönliche Gesundheitstipps produziert. Die jährlichen Kosten für die Nutzung der aktuellen Version sind moderat. Man kann die App auch ohne Anbindung an individuelle Daten nutzen. Dann sind die Klänge bei verschiedenen Personen gleich.

App gezielt blockieren zu können ist auch so unglaublich nützlich und sinnvoll. Over alle eine klare Empfehlung.

relax/unwind/calm-down.title: Tolle App, aber….
relax/unwind/calm-down.content: Die App ist wirklich sehr toll und sehr gut durchdacht, insbesondere für Menschen, die nur ganz leichte Fokussierung Entspannung oder Relaxation brauchen verbunden mit minimaler Aktivität, so dass man nicht dabei einschläft! relax/unwind/calm-down.title: Abzocke

relax/unwind/calm-down.title: No feed, no scroll. Unwind, relax.

relax/unwind/calm-down.content:
Ich habe die App auf meinem IPhone benutzt und fand Sie wirklich super, doch als ich im Relaxmodus die Blockierten Apps angestellt habe um halt Ruhe in der Relax Zeit zu erhalten ist mein Handy nur noch am spinnen!!!!! relax/unwind/calm-down.title: Fokus, Flow und feiner Sound.
relax/unwind/calm-down.content: Endel ist genau das, was ich gesucht habe. Super durchdachtes Design, intuitiv zu bedienen und absolut minimalistisch im besten Sinne. Die Klangwelten sind nicht nur atmosphärisch stark, sondern helfen mir tatsächlich, konzentriert zu bleiben – ob beim Arbeiten, Lesen oder einfach nur Abschalten. Besonders die Fokus-Beats sind top. relax/unwind/calm-down.title: KI Stimme für 60€

relax/unwind/calm-down.title: Entspannt, entstresst und konzentriert wie noch nie :-)
relax/unwind/calm-down.content: Endel ist die beste App, die ich jemals gekauft habe. Jeden Cent zig mal wert. Es ist wie eine Massage für meine Seele. Danke für diese wundervolle App.

relax/unwind/calm-down.title: Sehr entspannend!
relax/unwind/calm-down.content:
Seit einiger Zeit entwickelt sich Endel meiner Meinung nach zum Schlechteren. Die App wird immer unübersichtlicher. Man kann dieselben Dinge an zig Verschiedenen Stellen auswählen und muss oft hin und her wischen oder tippen, um an die richtige Stelle für andere Dinge zu gelangen.

Gerade die Einfachheit und das simple Design der App haben mir immer sehr gefallen. Mittlerweile wirkt die App überfrachtet. Ironischerweise ist der Inhalt gar nicht mehr geworden – bloß die Bedienung wurde verkompliziert. 

Jetzt kommt aber auch noch dazu, dass die App fehlerhaft ist. Wenn ich z.B. im Bereich „Entdecken“ vertikal scrollen möchte, dann passiert entweder gar nichts oder der Bereich schließt sich. Horizontal kann ich dort teilweise gar nicht scrollen. 

Aber immerhin gelange ich trotzdem ans Ziel, weil ich ja noch die anderen beiden Wege zum Auswählen des Modus nutzen kann … Ironie. 

Vorherige Rezension:
Die Sounds dieser App sind wirklich toll! Dank der vier Modi kann man zwischen sehr zurückhaltenden Klängen und solchen Klängen wählen, die rhythmisch sind. Bei anderen Apps, die einen mit Ambient-Sounds versorgen, bekommt man häufig das Gefühl „jetzt reicht‘s mir langsam“ und schaltet sie ab. Dieses Gefühl bekommt man bei Endel nie, da die Klänge ausreichend variiert werden, weil unter anderem Wetter und Uhrzeit als Eingangsparameter für die Klangauswahl/-erzeugung dienen.

relax/unwind/calm-down.title: Wow

reading/writing.title: Unethical strategies to make it nearly impossible to cancel
reading/writing.content:
I signed up for a seven day trial, and when I signed up, I immediately went to cancel so I wouldn’t forget to do so before the trial period was up if I didn’t want to continue it. When I went to cancel it immediately, there was even place to mark why I was canceling now, and one of their options was “so I wouldn’t forget”. Despite immediately having cancelled, I today that I would be charged tomorrow. So I went onto the app to cancel. Going to the “contact support“ section tells you to go to settings and hit manage subscriptions and there you will see “cancel subscriptions“ - but that is not written there. The layout of that page is misleadingly organized, with “unsubscribe“ at the bottom, situated to make you think you’re unsubscribing from communications, not canceling your subscription. Long story short, went through multiple avenues following their false steps to cancel, sent down different rabbit holes; sending the email on the “contact support page“ did not work, and eventually I just went back to that settings page and went to the bottom to hit unsubscribe. Well THAT is actually where you cancel your subscription! But then they interrupt that process by asking you to take a survey. If you x out of the survey, it ends your cancellation process. You have to start over again, you have to open the browser window for the survey, then you have to click several more times in the app to confirm you want to cancel. 
One of the most unethical and convoluted strategies of ever come across to make it difficult for consumers to cancel. Should be illegal. If we can all sign up to pay with one click, we should be able to cancel with one click.

reading/writing.title: Misleading advertising

reading/writing.title: Scam
reading/writing.content:
After canceling my subscription 4 years ago, Endel has continued charge me without notice.  I have verified that I am a free subscriber in the app, Endel is not in my list of managed subscriptions, nor have i received any notification about having a subscription or warning that I am about to be charged. 

After contacting (AI bot) support, they basically said there is nothing they can do because it's been over 31 days. Period.  No explanation to how or why these charges occurred.  

Avoid!

Edit: after writing this review, I received another response from "the developer"/bit saying the EXACT same thing about the 30 day window for a refund.  Let me be clear, not only was I paying for this service for 2 years without authorization, but my account was operating under the free subscription and I could not access the pro features if I wanted. 

Endel was probably a cool app 5 years ago but is clearly operating in auto mode that does not implement a path to resolving user issues.

focus/work.title: Latest Mac release is a catchup, not a well designed product
focus/work.content:
Endel is a “no brainer” when it comes to finding an ambient soundtrack to accompany your areas of focus in life, however the latest Mac release falls short in design and usability. This latest version feels merely like an attempt at catching up to the iOS versions feature set, while sacrificing usability and adding lots of annoyances.

The app used to seamlessly mix and flow between sound sets as you adjusted the mood to your liking. Now the sound just abruptly stops before advancing, making the app feel more like an audio player and not something well crafted.

It is not as fast and responsive as it used to be, and takes a while to load up the main features. It should really be more snappy, and the controls and main features should be within the first 1-2 clicks of opening the app.

I’m not sure if this is a poorly executed Electron app translation of what used to feel more Mac native. I hope the developers can make the app more of a first-class experience that we strive for on the Mac.

tinnitus/noise-masking.title: It works
tinnitus/noise-masking.content:
This was recommended to me by an ADHDer who swore by it.
I’ve used a lot of different binaural soundscapes. Usually I don’t believe in the legitimacy of them but for some reason this one helps me focus when I need to do my morning pages and regular writing. 
I like how it lets you easily skip to another track if the one being offered to you isn’t helpful / too distracting.
I love the deep work option and I’ve tried the section to help with sleep- but the deep work (inside the focus section) is the best. 
My noise canceling headphones died so I’ve been just playing this through my phone speakers- even then it still works (although I prefer the headphones- after I’ve been listening to anything on brain FM while wearing headphones as soon as I take them off, there is a noticeable “pop” in my ears- like I’ve just changed altitude)
A friend of mine had a headache and this app helped lessen its intensity. If you want a shortcut into flow state, then brain.fm is your friend. Worth the money!

tinnitus/noise-masking.title: Better than coffee!
tinnitus/noise-masking.content: Work, sleep or prayer this app is a must for us that struggle with long periods of focus or meditation. It replaced my Adderall and I drink much less coffee now. Used with noise canceling headphones…it’s a game changer. Highly recommended!

tinnitus/noise-masking.title: Better than
tinnitus/noise-masking.content:
I’m 23 weeks in using this app and it is my most important tool. I came to brain.fm for the variety and I stayed because I found I can actually focus. 

I’ve tried several things to calm my monkey mind and give it something to occupy itself with while I work, read or plan. I’ve had a waterfall on my desk physically and monitor virtually , I’ve listened to classical music (thank you Mozart), I’ve listened to white noise, tried brown noise, and I even bought an album with nothing but the sounds of a coffee shop (a favorite by the way) I’ve listened to more audiobooks than I can count(for the more repetitive tasks).  I’ve even tried working on my computer in VR to shut out distractions (how much battery do I have left?)

I tried brain.fm because the coffee shop was getting old but I’ve found that (coupled with noise canceling headphones or even regular earbuds), I can sit at the kitchen table in the middle of life happening and still focus on what I’m doing.  Where my wife walking by used to throw me off, now I barely notice.  It’s almost like VR. I’ve also been attacking my distractibility from other angles but, I was using brain.fm before that. 

As I’ve used it I gradually added in or took away certain sounds. I’ve liked what I liked and thumb downed what I didn’t (the evil drone didn’t work for me) I’ve done the meditation, I tried sleep but it pulled a Pink Floyd Dark Side of the Moon and scared me awake after lulling me off, easily fixable with a thumb down. 

Thank you guys for a great app and the work you’ve put into it. If the science is just a scam don’t tell me about it because it’s been working great for me.  I suspect there has to be something to the science though because every now and then I stop and realize “I’ve been working on this for 2 hours?”

And then I can stay there in the zone for a long, long time. It’s the next best thing to hyper focus I haven’t tried the music for insomnia or anxiety yet. However, I did find the relax and wind down music quite good after a long day of focus on work.

adhd/neurodivergent.title: My brain needs Brain.fm daily to focus
adhd/neurodivergent.content:
If you have a neurodivergent brain, this app is a lifesaver! 

For work, I listen to "Deep Focus" on my desktop computer every single day when I have to lock in and accomplish my tasks. In total silence, my brain goes off on tangents, but when I use brain.FM, it occupies the "wandering" or distracted part of my brain with non-lyric, interesting, non-repetitive looping jams so I can actually get things done.

For household tasks, or if I'm having trouble getting moving in the mornings, I use the "Motivation" music, and for whatever reason, it gets my toes tapping and helps me tidy, declutter, and finish chores with no struggling.

When I'm anxious or getting ready for a presentation or event, I listen to "Destress" while I'm preparing to calm my nerves.

At night, I listen to "Wind Down" or "Deep Sleep" to relax before bed.

Right now I'm on an 86-week streak of using this app in so many settings of my life, and I truly couldn't function without it. I recommend it to everyone I know who has ADHD or focus issues – it's exactly what I need to get things done!

adhd/neurodivergent.title: Definitely helps my ADHD focus issues at least a bit!
adhd/neurodivergent.content:
This app hasn’t been a transformative, life-changing discovery like some ads suggest, but I’ve been using it for over half a year now and I definitely notice some improvement in my focus and attention when using it! Exactly how much of a difference depends on the day/time/circumstances, but it’s enough that this has become a regular ADHD management tool for me, for everything from studying to working on creative projects, really anything that I need a focus boost for. 

The most significant improvement for me happens when my brain is hitting that boredom-burnout point on long assignments or study sessions. Putting on the music in this app helps get my brain out of the disengaged/distracted slump, or at least reduces how bad it is. If I was already having a relatively good focus day I don’t notice as much impact; I’m sure there’s still at least little, but it’s less obvious. 

As a side note, I’m really glad the app has the thumbs down button permanently skip songs. I have some misophonia and there have been several songs that had just the wrong combination of sounds in order to trigger it, but being able to simply remove those songs from rotation means that’s not a serious problem. 

I do wish there was a way to have playlists in addition to the favorites library though…

I zoned out faster then normal and stayed zoned out until a coworker called my name on the walkie. I came to with dogs playing crazily! 

This app dulls your senses it might be great for office work or a job that is rhythmic but if your job requires you to be alert and aware such as fast food, operating heavy machinery, any work with kids or animals, being on an active construction zone. Ect. This is not the app for you! 

Worst part was after the music my alert senses were COMPLETELY GONE THE WHOLE DAY!

This app does work but it’s not going to enhance your awareness it’s going to reduce it!!!!

If you are prone to daydreaming or getting lost in thought DO NOT USE THIS APP IN A MOMENT YOU NEED TO BE ALERT IN!

Great app. Not what I was expecting.

Most people would likely be satisfied with just simply liking or disliking a particular track that the program chooses for you based on the ‘task’ you’re choosing.

sleep.title: At the end brain.fm wins without any doubts
sleep.content:
I’ve always listened to this tracks and brain.fm was always boring with so much repetition, random subscriptions, random new tracks…and so on. This app is basically designed to make you disciplined and healthy. It may have some tracks you dislike (that’s of course the reason they have a dislike option too). Brain.fm actually did a lot of things for me: it managed to cure brain fog, it cured depression, my results on exams weren’t just good they were excellent. My life style has been changing, this music options and tactics make it possible for me to win in sport tournaments by for instance meditating before the tournament, sleeping with the sleep/ relax music doesn’t only trigger long good sleep, I somehow started waking up early and seizing the day like a hunter its prey. Brain.fm is a weapon actually that might look at first glance random and not useful, but when you actually do activities with this music and lock in focused, life may become not so colorful and joyful like it was when no discipline was there, but it unleashes your fighting spirit, your working spirit, working feels like you go in another dimension of how focused you are. Best regards Viktor Markovic

focus/work.title: Theres A Critical Flaw
focus/work.content:
Personally, I find it remarkably short-sighted on the part of the marketing and development teams to take such a low-resolution risk. I always appreciate a preliminary trial period—it’s a necessary means of developing initial rapport with an app. However, the experience within that trial is everything.

While the content itself is lovely and the interface reasonably well-organized, the experience is undermined by what feels like an overly aggressive sales tactic. Each time the app is reopened, users are met with a full-page subscription prompt—effectively shouting “BUY, BUY, BUY” in their faces. It’s not only excessive; it’s uncomfortable. Literally every time you close or switch between apps, you’re forced to navigate through this.

I have no objection to a business earning revenue, but how you go about it reveals what truly motivates you. If user experience is so readily disrupted by profit-driven interruptions, then user wellbeing clearly isn’t the priority. The focus, quite plainly, is on maximizing subscriptions. If that weren’t the case, this constant paywall push wouldn’t exist—or at least would be more thoughtfully implemented. And that isn’t actually the issue; profit is critical, obviously. But this is a poor strategy, considering how simple of a mistake it is. I promise—regardless of what statistics you’re using—this is a low-resolution mistake aimed at short-term gain, not long-term success.

And that leads me to the core concern: if I can’t trust the intent behind your methods, how can I trust the integrity of your content? I’ve enjoyed the music, and I think there’s real potential within the model itself—the app has even complemented my workflow—but it’s difficult to fully invest in something that treats trust as secondary to conversion rates, and does so so casually and carelessly. You could have at least hidden the intent to some degree—or at all.

You could do better—and frankly, you should want to.

focus/work.title: Brain.fm concept works - the app not!
focus/work.content:
I really believe in the concept behind Brain.fm — it genuinely helps me focus and be more productive. The core product works, and I’ve seen real benefits from using it.

However, the app itself is the reason I’m cancelling my membership.

The usability is extremely frustrating. The interface feels unintuitive and inconsistent, especially compared to other major apps that have already figured out what works well for users. It would make a big difference to follow more established design patterns instead of reinventing basic interactions.

The offline mode is particularly problematic — it’s barely usable and difficult to understand. For a product that people rely on in various environments, this should be much more reliable and straightforward.

Overall, the app feels like it hasn’t been properly tested with real users. There are too many friction points in everyday use.

It’s disappointing because the underlying concept is strong, but the app experience doesn’t support it.

timer / scheduling / session features.title: Ein wirklich gelungenes Programm
timer / scheduling / session features.content:
Die App verbindet die physischen Daten des Nutzers (wenn eine Smartwatch benutzt wird) mit den kosmischen (zirkardianrhythmisch) - und zwar regionalspezifisch (Wetterapp und Standortdaten). Sie spielt Klänge über einen Synthesizer ab. Vier Klangprogramme bilden die eingespeisten Daten ab. Dabei gibt es vier frei wählbare Klangvarianten - je nachdem, was man erreichen will: Beruhigung (Rest) Konzentration (Fokus), Ab- oder Anspannung (Go to) und schließlich Schlaf (Sleep). Es gibt im Internet eine Variante mit Gesang. Die sollte in die App integriert werden. Interessant wäre sicher auch die Kopplung mit einem Emotions-/ Gehirnwellensensor (Stirnband). Drittens schlage ich vor, dass ein Expertenmodus eingebaut wird, der Nutzungsempfehlungen und Verhaltensempfehlungen sowie persönliche Gesundheitstipps produziert. Die jährlichen Kosten für die Nutzung der aktuellen Version sind moderat. Man kann die App auch ohne Anbindung an individuelle Daten nutzen. Dann sind die Klänge bei verschiedenen Personen gleich.

offline / download.title: Endel continues to soothe and focus my brain
offline / download.content: I found Endel when it first came out, 2017 or so. I struggled with technical issues on my ancient phone but loved when it worked. While off grid in the woods for 2 weeks, this became my soundtrack on my iphone 12 mini, which I still use. At that point endel worked offline, with the most basic sounds free and no 10 minute limit. It was incredible and non-invasive in the natural space. I also used it at night on low volume to warn the cougars and bears of my presence. I didn't die! Yay! I finally purchased a year of it now, in 2026, because I need it more than ever being finally diagnosed with adhd and autism. I love focus, move and sleep-I love the way it supports my odd hours or focus and helps me rest easily for sleep. When I turn it off, I almost feel like I was being physically pushed and then, like the push is gone when I turn it off. It actually supports focus, aligns with neuroplasticity experiments and is simply my fave thing to listen to for all activities! It's expensive and I wish it was more accessible for lower income people. But even the free version is super helpful. LOVE IT!

customization / mix-your-own / controls.title: Definitely helps my ADHD focus issues at least a bit!
customization / mix-your-own / controls.content:
This app hasn’t been a transformative, life-changing discovery like some ads suggest, but I’ve been using it for over half a year now and I definitely notice some improvement in my focus and attention when using it! Exactly how much of a difference depends on the day/time/circumstances, but it’s enough that this has become a regular ADHD management tool for me, for everything from studying to working on creative projects, really anything that I need a focus boost for. 

The most significant improvement for me happens when my brain is hitting that boredom-burnout point on long assignments or study sessions. Putting on the music in this app helps get my brain out of the disengaged/distracted slump, or at least reduces how bad it is. If I was already having a relatively good focus day I don’t notice as much impact; I’m sure there’s still at least little, but it’s less obvious. 

As a side note, I’m really glad the app has the thumbs down button permanently skip songs. I have some misophonia and there have been several songs that had just the wrong combination of sounds in order to trigger it, but being able to simply remove those songs from rotation means that’s not a serious problem. 

I do wish there was a way to have playlists in addition to the favorites library though…

For me, I found sounds like static and crinkling to be anxiety triggering and wish I could have filtered out layers of such sound as I can with other sleep soundscape apps. No value found for me, especially for a paid subscription required app.
